subject: Post-call: SLO clarifications + customer-led k6 run scheduling
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Tan <samuel.t@pegasus.ai>, QA Team <qa@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: SLO clarifications + customer-led k6 run scheduling

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and the concrete next steps so we can get the customer-led k6 dry run scheduled. I captured what we discussed around SLOs and the test requirements below. Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Summary (as discussed)
- Target latency SLOs: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 250ms for requests up to 128 tokens; tail (p99) target <= 450ms during steady window.
- Throughput: baseline target 120 req/s sustained across the cluster; allow short bursts up to 200 req/s for 60s.
- Concurrency / streaming: customer expects ~60 concurrent streaming sessions (server-sent events / long-polling) with average chunk latency < 200ms.
- Streaming specifics: 1-2 tokens per chunk, keep-alive ping every 30s.

Customer-led test asks we agreed on
1) Pegasus will run k6 from their infra using our test account and scripts.
2) Pegasus will add our runner IPs to their allowlist (IPs below).
3) Redwood provides a short-lived test API key and a k6 starter script.
4) We'll observe and capture token-level latency, KV-cache hit rate, and per-route error breakdown.

Proposed allowlist (please add these to your firewall for the test window):
- 34.209.112.45
- 34.210.67.11
- 34.211.90.122
- 3.128.14.250

Proposed test window (UTC): Aug 11, 2026 02:00 - 05:00 UTC (US-friendly overnight slot) — can you confirm this works for your QA team?

What I will attach / share now:
- k6 starter script (k6_script_v3.js) with a recommended traffic profile.
- A JSON traffic profile you can import (pegasus_k6_profile.json).
- A short-lived test account credential file (redwood_test_account_creds.txt) — we will rotate after the run.

Next steps / asks for Pegasus
- Confirm the Aug 11 window or propose alternatives.
- Confirm the allowlist has been applied and who on your side will own the test (name + email).
- If you need different traffic shapes (burstier or longer tails), send a sample CSV of expected QPS over time.

I'll loop in Monica and Grace to coordinate the script and logging hooks. Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: Samuel Tan <samuel.t@pegasus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: QA Team <qa@pegasus.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO clarifications + customer-led k6 run scheduling

Thanks Karthik — useful summary. A couple of quick notes from QA:
- The Aug 11 window looks OK on our side but I need to get final sign-off from infra; can you hold that as tentative?
- We'll own the k6 execution but will need the starter script and the test account. Our QA lead is Maya R. (maya.r@pegasus.ai) — I'll loop her in after I confirm the window.
- Can you also share an example traffic matrix (QPS over time) so our infra team can provision and budget network egress?

One question: for streaming, are you recommending we use your server-sent-events endpoint or the websocket path you mentioned? We currently prefer SSE for simplicity but can run websocket if required.

I'll add the allowlist request to our change window ticket once you confirm the IPs are final.

—Samuel
Principal Product Manager, Pegasus AI
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Tan <samuel.t@pegasus.ai>, Maya R. <maya.r@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: k6 profile + notes for Pegasus dry run

Hi Samuel / Maya — looping in the k6 details and a short checklist so QA can pick this up quickly. Attachments: pegasus_k6_profile.json (traffic profile), k6_script_v3.js (script). Also adding the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/pegasus/k6_scripts/k6_script_v3.js

Quick notes:
- The attached k6 profile runs a 30m ramp (0 -> 120 rps), 30m steady at 120 rps, then a 5m burst to 200 rps. You can adjust durations locally.
- For streaming, the k6 script uses SSE client implementation (we added a simple SSE helper) — SSE is preferred for parity with your current infra; websocket branch is in the Drive if you prefer.
- We log the per-request token payload size and attach a short header "X-Redwood-Test: pegasus-dryrun" so we can filter traces.
- Please ensure your infra allows the runner IPs listed and that outgoing TLS termination does not strip the test header.

If you want us to run the k6 from our hosted runner instead of your infra, we can do that as well (sometimes helpful for troubleshooting), but for this dry run you requested a customer-led execution so we've prepared these artifacts.

Cheers — Monica
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Tan <samuel.t@pegasus.ai>, Maya R. <maya.r@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: k6 profile + notes for Pegasus dry run

Thanks Monica — and thanks Samuel for the quick reply. Two small clarifications from our side before you lock the change window:
1) IP allowlist: the four IPs listed in my original email are final for our runners for this dry run (they're NATed). If you prefer we can provide a CIDR instead, but many customers prefer explicit addresses.
2) Test account: attached is a short-lived API key file (redwood_test_account_creds.txt). The key is scoped to read/generate and expires 48 hours after the run. Do not check it into source control.

Operational notes we will monitor actively during the run:
- p50/p95/p99 per-route latency and per-token time (we'll share a short dashboard link once the run starts).
- Error rate per HTTP status and model fallback counts.
- KV-cache hit rate (to show prefix/cache effectiveness).

If anything changes on your scheduling side, please propose two alternate 3-hour windows within the week of Aug 10-16. Otherwise we'll tentatively hold Aug 11 02:00-05:00 UTC.

Attachments: k6_script_v3.js, redwood_test_account_creds.txt (short-lived)

Thanks — Karthik
From: Samuel Tan <samuel.t@pegasus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-06T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: k6 profile + notes for Pegasus dry run

Confirmed — infra has applied the four IPs to our allowlist and Maya (maya.r@pegasus.ai) will own the execution. We've created JIRA ticket PGA-412 to track the run and approvals.

We will proceed with the Aug 11, 02:00-05:00 UTC window. Maya will reach out separately with the k6 run command and any small tweaks to the steady-state duration.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — Samuel
Principal Product Manager, Pegasus AI
